item.title: Epstein survivors release Super Bowl ad demanding DOJ transparency
item.description:
On Super Bowl Sunday, survivors of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse released an emotional public service announcement calling on Attorney General Pam Bondi to release the remaining files from the federal investigation into the late convicted sex offender, directly challenging President Donald Trump's recent suggestion that the country should "get on to something else."

The 33-second video, produced by the anti-trafficking organization World Without Exploitation, features several survivors holding photographs of themselves as teenagers when they were abused by Epstein. The ad opens with text stating, "On November 19, 2025, the Epstein Files Transparency Act was signed into law. 3 Million Files Still Have Not Been Released."

item.title: Hong Kong sentences Jimmy Lai to 20 years under security law
item.description:
A Hong Kong court on Monday sentenced pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison, the harshest penalty yet under Beijing's national security law, in a case that has drawn sharp international condemnation and heightened concerns over the erosion of press freedom in the former British colony.

Three government-appointed judges handed down the sentence for the 78-year-old founder of the now-defunct Apple Daily newspaper, who was convicted in December on two counts of conspiracy to collude with foreign forces and one count of conspiracy to publish seditious materials. Judge Esther Toh ruled that 18 years should be served consecutively to Lai's existing fraud sentence, meaning he could remain behind bars for the rest of his life.

item.title: Taiwan calls US demand to shift 40% of chip capacity 'impossible'
item.description:
Taiwan's top tariff negotiator has declared that relocating 40 percent of the island's semiconductor manufacturing capacity to the United States would be "impossible," pushing back against American officials who have called for a major production shift in recent weeks.

Vice Premier Cheng Li-chiun, who led Taiwan's recent trade negotiations with Washington, said in an interview with Taiwanese television channel CTS broadcast late Sunday that she had clearly conveyed to US officials that Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem, developed over decades, cannot simply be uprooted.

"I have made it very clear to the United States that this is impossible," Cheng said, referring to the 40 percent target that US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has publicly floated.

item.title: IMO committee convenes on Arctic shipping fuel rules
item.description:
As melting Arctic sea ice opens new shipping routes, four nations are pressing the International Maritime Organization to mandate cleaner fuels for vessels transiting polar waters, aiming to reduce black carbon emissions that accelerate ice melt.

Denmark, France, Germany, and the Solomon Islands have submitted a proposal to the IMO's Pollution Prevention and Response committee, which convened in London on February 9, requiring ships operating in the Arctic to use "polar fuels"—lighter distillate fuels that produce less soot than the residual fuels commonly used by maritime vessels.

item.title: Nikkei hits record high as election wins spark Asian rally
item.description:
Stock markets across Asia rallied sharply on Monday as investors cheered decisive election victories in Japan and Thailand over the weekend, with political clarity sparking a wave of risk appetite that sent Tokyo's benchmark index to all-time highs.

Japan's Nikkei 225 soared past 57,000 for the first time in history, hitting an intraday peak of 57,337.07, after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's Liberal Democratic Party secured a historic supermajority in Sunday's snap election. The LDP won 316 of the 465 seats in the Lower House—the most ever claimed by a single party in Japan's postwar history—giving Takaichi an overwhelming mandate to pursue her economic and security agenda.

item.title: EU threatens emergency action to force Meta to reopen WhatsApp to AI rivals
item.description:
The European Commission issued a formal warning to Meta on Monday, threatening to impose emergency measures that would force the tech giant to allow rival artificial intelligence chatbots back onto WhatsApp while an antitrust investigation continues.

EU regulators delivered a "statement of objections" to Meta, setting out a preliminary finding that the company breached competition rules by blocking third-party AI assistants from accessing its messaging platform. The move escalates a probe launched in December 2025 following Meta's decision to ban general-purpose AI chatbots from WhatsApp's business tools.

item.title: Kremlin says it's in talks to aid Cuba amid US 'suffocating' sanctions
item.description:
The Kremlin on Monday accused the United States of imposing "suffocating measures" on Cuba and pledged to continue discussions with Havana on providing energy assistance, even as the United Kingdom threatens military action against the Russian tankers that would deliver such aid.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that "the situation is really critical in Cuba" and that Russia is "negotiating with our Cuban friends to find potential solutions to these issues, at least to give what help we can." The statement comes days after Russian Ambassador to Cuba Viktor Coronelli confirmed to state news agency RIA Novosti that Moscow's oil shipments to the island would persist despite Washington's warnings of tariffs on countries supplying fuel to the Caribbean nation.

item.title: China warns Japan of 'resolute response' after Takaichi landslide
item.description:
Beijing issued a sharp warning to Tokyo on Monday, urging Japan to retract Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's November remarks about potential military intervention over Taiwan, as China-Japan tensions escalate following her decisive election victory.

"If the far-right forces in Japan misjudge the situation and act recklessly, they will inevitably face resistance from the Japanese people and a resolute response from the international community," Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said at a regular news conference on February 9. He added that Japan must "demonstrate basic sincerity in safeguarding the political foundation of China-Japan relations through concrete actions."

item.title: Norwegian ambassador resigns over Epstein ties as scandal spreads
item.description: The release of millions of Jeffrey Epstein documents by the U.S. Department of Justice on January 30 has sent shockwaves through political establishments across multiple continents, forcing resignations and triggering investigations from Norway to France to Slovakia, while the response in the United States remains comparatively muted.

item.title: Discord to require face scans or IDs for full access in March
item.description:
Discord announced on Sunday that all users worldwide will be placed into a restricted "teen-by-default" experience starting in early March, requiring age verification through a face scan or government ID to unlock full platform access.

The gaming and chat platform, which has more than 200 million monthly active users, said the move is part of enhanced teen safety features timed to coincide with Safer Internet Day. Users who do not complete verification will face blurred sensitive content, blocked access to age-restricted channels and servers, and restricted direct message settings.

item.title: Starmer faces mounting calls to resign after top aides depart
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is fighting for his political survival after two senior Downing Street officials resigned within 24 hours and the Scottish Labour leader publicly called for him to step down.

Tim Allan, Starmer's director of communications, resigned on Monday, just one day after chief of staff Morgan McSweeney departed, plunging the government deeper into crisis over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as UK ambassador to the United States despite his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar became the most senior Labour politician to demand Starmer's resignation, declaring at a hastily arranged press conference in Glasgow: "The distraction needs to end and the leadership in Downing Street has to change". Sarwar warned that failures at the heart of Downing Street were jeopardizing Labour's chances in the May Scottish parliamentary elections.

item.title: UN says 53 migrants dead or missing after boat sinks off Libya
item.description:
A rubber dinghy carrying 55 migrants capsized off the coast of Libya early Friday, leaving at least 53 people dead or missing, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration reported Monday. Two babies were among those lost in what the agency described as "yet another deadly incident along the Central Mediterranean route."

Only two survivors, both Nigerian women, were rescued by Libyan authorities following a search-and-rescue operation. One woman reported losing her husband, while the other said she lost her two children in the tragedy. IOM teams provided emergency medical care to the survivors upon their disembarkation.

item.title: China tells banks to cut US Treasury holdings, citing market risks
item.description: Chinese regulators have quietly advised domestic financial institutions to limit new purchases of US government bonds and begin reducing existing holdings, citing concerns over concentration risks and market volatility, according to Bloomberg. The directive, issued in recent weeks to major lenders, sent Treasury yields higher and the dollar lower as markets opened Monday.

item.title: Scientists detect first underground lava tube on Venus
item.description: Researchers at the University of Trento in Italy have identified the first subsurface feature ever detected on Venus: a massive lava tube beneath a shield volcano in the planet's northern hemisphere. The finding, published Monday in the journal Nature Communications, provides direct evidence of underground volcanic structures on Earth's neighboring planet, previously only theorized by scientists.

item.title: Uber to buy Turkish delivery startup Getir for $435 million
item.description:
Uber Technologies announced Monday it has agreed to acquire the delivery operations of Turkish rapid-delivery startup Getir from Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Company, marking the ride-hailing giant's latest push to expand its food delivery footprint in the Middle East.

The deal, pending regulatory approval, covers Getir's full delivery portfolio in Türkiye, including food, grocery, retail, and water delivery services. Under the terms, Uber will pay $335 million in cash to acquire 100 percent of Getir's food delivery business and invest an additional $100 million for a 15 percent stake in the grocery, retail, and water operations, with a complete acquisition of the remaining delivery portfolio expected over the coming years based on performance conditions.

item.title: Ukraine exposes 21 Russian drone makers, says most unsanctioned
item.description:
Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) has published new data identifying 21 Russian companies involved in developing and producing drones for Russia's war against Ukraine, with officials highlighting that more than half of the listed firms remain free from international sanctions.

The data, released on the HUR's War & Sanctions portal, names manufacturers responsible for producing a range of unmanned aerial vehicles currently deployed against Ukrainian forces and civilians, including cargo drones, first-person-view (FPV) attack drones, and AI-enabled kamikaze systems.

item.title: Eight Muslim nations condemn Israel's West Bank annexation moves
item.description:
Eight predominantly Muslim countries issued a joint statement on Monday condemning Israel's newly approved measures in the occupied West Bank, calling them illegal annexation attempts that violate international law and threaten regional stability.

The foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates denounced Israel's Sunday decision as an effort to impose "unlawful Israeli sovereignty, entrenching settlement activity, and enforcing a new legal and administrative reality in the occupied West Bank, thereby accelerating attempts at its illegal annexation and the displacement of the Palestinian people."

The joint statement, posted on the Turkish Foreign Ministry's website, emphasized that "Israel has no sovereignty over the occupied Palestinian territory" and warned that such actions "fuel violence and conflict in the region."

item.title: Trump to visit China in April for Xi summit
item.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing during the first week of April for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to a Politico report citing three people familiar with the plans. The trip would mark the first visit by a sitting American president to China since Trump's own 2017 state visit during his first term.

The visit comes as the world's two largest economies seek to stabilize relations following months of trade tensions, including an $11 billion U.S. arms deal with Taiwan and Chinese military exercises surrounding the island. Trump has described the upcoming trip as a "business trip" aimed at securing further trade wins.

item.title: US, Bangladesh sign trade deal cutting tariffs to 19%
item.description: The United States and Bangladesh have signed a trade agreement reducing US tariffs on Bangladeshi goods to 19 percent and establishing a mechanism for duty-free treatment of certain apparel products made with American materials. The deal, finalized Monday, comes just days before Bangladesh holds its first general election since the ouster of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024.

item.title: Mexico suspends oil shipments to Cuba to avoid US tariffs
item.description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed on Monday that Mexico has suspended oil shipments to Cuba to avoid tariffs threatened by the Trump administration, calling the US sanctions "very unfair" as she warned that the measures would "strangle" the crisis-stricken island nation.

"This sanction being imposed on countries that sell oil to Cuba is very unfair... sanctions that harm the people are not right," Sheinbaum told reporters at her daily press briefing. "You cannot strangle a people like this—it's very unfair, very unfair."
